judged_text: Duplicate-guest detection compares the submitted email case-sensitively against booking.attendees and does not normalize case, while the blacklist comparison lowercases only the blacklist entries, not the guest email. Adding 'User@Example.com' when 'user@example.com' is already an attendee creates a duplicate Attendee row for the same person (duplicate DB rows and a duplicate attendee on the calendar event), and a guest email listed in BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS with different casing bypasses the blacklist and still gets booked and emailed.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, duplicate detection and blacklist checks are case-sensitive: `!booking.attendees.some((attendee) => guest === attendee.email)` and `!blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)`. The blacklist is lowercased (`.map((email) => email.toLowerCase())`) but `guest` is not, so casing differences can bypass the blacklist. Similarly, an existing attendee `user@example.com` won’t block adding `User@Example.com`, potentially creating a duplicate attendee row and propagating to calendar/email logic.
